exercises.name: Push-Up
steps: Place your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, directly under your shoulders.
Extend your legs back so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Lower your chest toward the floor, keeping elbows at about 45° from your body.
Push back up until your arms are straight, without locking the elbows hard.
mistakes: Half reps that don't lower the chest
exercises.safety: Too hard? Do them with hands on a bench or wall, or from your knees. Stop if you feel wrist or shoulder pain.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
steps: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Push your hips back and bend your knees as if sitting into a chair.
Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and heels flat on the floor.
Lower until thighs are around parallel (or as deep as you can with good form), then drive up through your whole foot.
exercises.safety: Master bodyweight squats before adding a barbell. Use a box behind you to learn depth. Stop if you feel knee or back pain.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
steps: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands.
Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Keep elbows pointing down and chest tall.
Squat down between your legs, pushing knees out over your toes.
Pause at the bottom, then stand up by driving through your feet.
mistakes: Letting the weight pull you forward
exercises.safety: Start light. This is a great way to learn squat technique before using a barbell.

exercises.name: Lunge
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Step forward (or backward for a reverse lunge) with one leg.
Lower your hips until both knees are bent about 90°, with the back knee hovering just above the floor.
Keep your front knee over your ankle, not pushed far past the toes or caving in.
Push through the front heel to return to standing, then switch legs.
mistakes: Short steps that overload the front knee
exercises.safety: Reverse lunges are usually easier on the knees for beginners. Hold onto support for balance if needed.

exercises.name: Plank
steps: Place forearms on the floor with elbows directly under shoulders.
Extend legs back, resting on your toes.
Form a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your abs, squeeze your glutes, and breathe steadily.
Hold for 20–30 seconds to start, building up over time.
mistakes: Looking up and straining the neck
exercises.safety: Quality beats duration. End the set when your form breaks. Do it from your knees if needed.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
Keep arms by your sides, palms down.
Brace your core and push through your heels to lift your hips.
Squeeze your glutes at the top so your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Lower slowly with control.
mistakes: Over-arching the lower back at the top
exercises.safety: Keep the movement controlled. If you feel it mostly in your lower back, tuck your ribs down and focus on the glutes.

exercises.name: Deadlift
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, bar over the middle of your feet.
Hinge at the hips and grip the bar just outside your legs.
Lower your hips, flatten your back, chest up, shoulders slightly over the bar.
Brace your core hard, then push the floor away and stand up, keeping the bar close to your legs.
Lock out by squeezing glutes, then lower by hinging at the hips first, then bending the knees.
mistakes: Bar drifting away from the body
Jerking the bar off the floor
Leaning back excessively at the top
exercises.safety: Learn it with light weight or a coach first. A rounded back under load is a common cause of injury. Stop if you feel back pain.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
steps: Stand holding the weights in front of your thighs, knees softly bent.
Push your hips back, sliding the weights down the front of your legs.
Keep your back flat and the weights close to your body.
Lower until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings (usually mid-shin).
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach lower
Bending the knees too much (turning it into a squat)
exercises.safety: Range of motion depends on hamstring flexibility. Don't force depth with a rounded back.

exercises.name: Bench Press
steps: Lie on the bench with eyes under the bar and feet flat on the floor.
Grip slightly wider than shoulder-width; pull shoulder blades back and down.
Unrack the bar and hold it over your shoulders with straight arms.
Lower it under control to your mid-chest with elbows at about 45–70° from your body.
Press back up to the starting position.
mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest
exercises.safety: Always use a spotter or safety arms when using a barbell, especially with heavier weights. Dumbbells are a safer way to start.

exercises.name: Overhead Shoulder Press
steps: Stand (or sit) tall holding weights at shoulder height, palms forward.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to avoid arching your back.
Press the weights straight overhead until arms are extended.
Keep your head neutral, moving it slightly back as the bar passes.
Lower under control back to shoulder height.
mistakes: Pressing forward instead of straight up
exercises.safety: Start light. Stop if you feel pinching in the shoulder.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
steps: Hang from the bar with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, palms facing away.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back to start the movement.
Pull yourself up by driving elbows toward your hips until your chin passes the bar.
Keep your body controlled; avoid swinging.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
mistakes: Shrugging shoulders up to the ears
exercises.safety: Can't do one yet? Use resistance bands, an assisted machine, lat pulldowns, or slow negatives (jump up, lower slowly).

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
steps: Sit with thighs secured under the pads and grip the bar wider than shoulder-width.
Lean back slightly with chest up.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving elbows down and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom.
Let the bar rise slowly until arms are straight.
mistakes: Leaning back too far and using momentum
exercises.safety: Control the weight up and down. Always pull to the front of your body.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
steps: Place one knee and hand on a bench, back flat and parallel to the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand with arm extended.
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, keeping the elbow close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blade at the top.
Lower under control and repeat, then switch sides.
mistakes: Twisting the torso to lift the weight
Pulling toward the shoulder instead of the hip
exercises.safety: Keep your spine neutral. Use a weight you can control without jerking.

exercises.name: Bicep Curl
steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows pinned close to your torso.
Curl the weights up toward your shoulders by bending at the elbow.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower slowly to full arm extension.
mistakes: Cutting the range of motion short
exercises.safety: Choose a weight you can lift without swinging. Stop if you feel elbow pain.

exercises.name: Dips
steps: Support yourself on parallel bars with arms straight and shoulders down.
Lean slightly forward and keep your core tight.
Lower by bending your elbows until upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Keep shoulders away from your ears.
Push back up to straight arms.
mistakes: Going too deep and straining the shoulders
exercises.safety: Beginners can start with bench dips (feet on floor) or an assisted dip machine. Stop if you feel pain in the front of the shoulder.

exercises.name: Burpee
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down and place your hands on the floor.
Jump or step your feet back into a plank position.
(Optional) Perform a push-up.
Jump or step your feet back toward your hands, then stand or jump up with arms overhead.
exercises.safety: Step back instead of jumping to make it low-impact. Pace yourself; burpees raise heart rate quickly.

exercises.name: Mountain Climber
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders.
Brace your core and keep your hips level.
Drive one knee toward your chest.
Quickly switch legs, like running in place.
Keep a steady rhythm while maintaining a straight back.
mistakes: Going so fast that form breaks
exercises.safety: Slow the tempo down if you lose control of your plank position.

exercises.name: Crunch
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Place fingertips lightly behind your ears or cross arms on your chest.
Exhale and curl your shoulders off the floor using your abs.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly with control.
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with your hands
Lifting all the way up with the hip flexors
exercises.safety: Keep your neck relaxed. Planks and dead bugs are good alternatives if crunches bother your neck or back.

exercises.name: Jumping Jacks
steps: Stand with feet together and arms at your sides.
Jump while spreading your feet wider than your hips and raising your arms overhead.
Jump back to the starting position.
Land softly on the balls of your feet.
Repeat at a steady pace.
exercises.safety: For a low-impact version, step one foot out at a time instead of jumping.

exercises.name: Wall Sit
steps: Stand with your back flat against a wall.
Walk your feet forward about two feet.
Slide down until your knees are bent around 90°.
Keep knees over ankles and back flat against the wall.
Hold for 20–45 seconds, breathing steadily.
exercises.safety: Hold a higher position (less knee bend) if 90° is too difficult or uncomfortable.
